title:
This type is used for encoding and decoding parts of URL strings. URL encoding rules are complex and idiosyncratic
so care must be taken to use the correct encoding:
 - "Path" encoding is for slash-separate paths (typically files). Slashes are _not_ encoded and spaces are encoded
   with "%20" (plus signs are not encoded). The #encodePath method does this.
 - "Query" encoding is for components of query strings and
   {@link https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods/POST form POST bodies}.
   Spaces may be encoded with either a '+' sign or "%20" and slashes will be encoded as "%2F". This should
   probably be called "query component" for clarity. The #encode method does this.

Here are the key differences between the encoding methods:

| Input   | Path | Path Component | Query Component |
|---------|------|----------------|-----------------|
| /       | /    | %2F            | %2F             |
| _space_ | %20  | %20            | +               |
| +       | +    | +              | %2B             |
| =       | =    | =              | %3D             |
| &       | &    | &              | %26             |

Note that #encode is very similar to JavaScript's
{@link https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/encodeURIComponent encodeURIComponent},
except that the latter uses "%20" for space instead of a plus sign.
name: UrlEncoder
